changes: Terrain fragment now mixes world-space macro/meso/micro noise with moisture, slope and altitude for continuous meadow, undergrowth soil and rock variation across clipmap levels.
Road asphalt noise uses rotated low-frequency world coordinates to remove repeated transverse striping; shoulder/verge widths reduced for a tighter ground transition.
Road segments procedurally add sparse timber guide rails with posts and twin beams, skipping bridge decks.

evidence.note: Chase frame shows continuous slope-following road, mixed grass/soil ground and readable timber edge detail; still behind bar in authored vegetation density and vehicle realism.
Autumn frame confirms multiscale terrain color continuity and reduced asphalt striping; fence remains darker and more regular than the bar's rustic wall.
Spring golden frame confirms road shoulder blend and natural rolling grade at a distant vista; atmospheric exposure and low-poly assets remain the largest gap.
Final summer frame: one-sided rails no longer dominate composition, asphalt reads as matte granular rather than repeated bands, terrain has visible meadow/soil patches.

remaining_gaps: Official references have authored high-detail vegetation and vehicle geometry beyond this scoped terrain/road pass.
Fence rails are still somewhat uniform along long straights; varied post spacing and occasional stone walls would improve regional specificity.
Road verge remains a broad graded strip in some lighting conditions due to the shared cross-section earthworks model.
